newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain to spend $477 mln on power, water projects.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain to spend $477 mln on power, water projects.

text.p: Bahrain plans to spend about 180 million dinars ($477 million) on new projects over the next four years to meet an increasing demand for electricity and water, a Bahraini minister said in remarks published on Tuesday.

The Gulf Daily News newspaper quoted Electricity and Water Minister Abdullah Mohammad Jumaa as saying the projects would be implemented within the framework of a 10-year plan prepared by British consultancy firm Mott MacDonald.
"The estimated cost of such projects over the coming four years is 180 million dinars," Jumaa said.
"We are confident to meet the ever-increasing demand for electricity and water through the construction of new projects, plant rehabilitation programmes and a conservation campaign."

Preliminary work had started on an estimated 150 million dinar power and water plant at Hidd, a village on Muharraq island which is linked with the capital Manama to the west by a three km (1.8 miles) causeway, Jumaa said.
Bahrain would spend about 25 million dinars on a submarine cable that would link the plant with the country's power network, he added.
Asea Brown Boveri AG would finance the project, which would be repaid by the government over 12 years, the daily quoted Jumaa as saying. It gave no further details.
"Bahrain's electricity production will increase by 280 megawatts and water production by 30 million gallons a day when the first phase of the Hidd project is completed by 1999," Jumaa said.
Production capacity stood at 1,210 megawatts this year.
Demand for electricity was expected to increase to 1,266 megawatts in the year 2000 and 1,629 megawatts in 2005 from 1,050 megawatts this year.
